decision: REVISE — Frozen decision_rule condition C3 fails (CI upper 0.2372 ≥ 0.15, TOST p_upper=0.286) and spec.json decision_rule maps CI upper ≥ 0.20 to FAIL. However, the audit identifies three confounds that make this failure indeterminate rather than a clean falsification of the orthogonality hypothesis under HTTP caching: (1) HTTP conditional caching was never operationally exercised — run_experiment.py never sends If-None-Match headers, so the 304/ETag code path in mock_server.py is untested; the experiment tests only declarative Cache-Control/ETag header presence, not operational HTTP caching; (2) n=240 is underpowered versus the parent n=480 (SE 0.065 vs 0.046, CI width ~0.25 vs ~0.18); the CI widening from 0.135 to 0.237 is partly a sample-size artifact, not solely an HTTP caching effect; (3) per-caching-mode heterogeneity is opposite to the hypothesis — cache_enabled r=-0.0055 (TOST PASS p=0.045 at delta=0.15) while cache_disabled r=0.217 (TOST FAIL), suggesting sampling noise or structural signal variance differences rather than HTTP caching as a common cause. The maximum justified claim is: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality at delta=0.15 is NOT confirmed on this evidence (pooled r=0.114, CI upper 0.237), but the failure is measurement-confounded and does NOT falsify the hypothesis that HTTP caching preserves orthogonality. C-FRESHNESS remains EXPERIMENTAL; no status advancement or rejection warranted. The parent's stochastic-mock orthogonality (r=0.046, CI upper 0.135 < 0.15) remains the established baseline — this experiment neither supersedes nor falsifies it.

reason: The frozen decision rule maps CI upper ≥ 0.20 to FAIL, and the observed CI upper 0.237 ≥ 0.20 satisfies this condition. However, the audit identifies that the failure is not a clean falsification of the orthogonality hypothesis under HTTP caching because: (1) the HTTP caching manipulation was incomplete — only declarative headers (Cache-Control, ETag generation) were tested; the operational conditional GET path (If-None-Match → 304) was never exercised by the client; (2) the sample size (n=240) is half the parent's (n=480), inflating SE from 0.046 to 0.065 and widening the CI from [−0.043, 0.135] to [−0.013, 0.237]; (3) the per-caching-mode heterogeneity (cache_enabled r=−0.0055 PASS vs cache_disabled r=0.217 FAIL) is opposite to the hypothesis that HTTP caching introduces coupling — if anything, the cache-enabled condition is cleaner. The maximum justified claim is that orthogonality is not confirmed under this specific (incomplete, underpowered) HTTP caching test, not that HTTP caching breaks orthogonality. The parent's PASS on stochastic mock (r=0.046, CI upper 0.135 < 0.15) remains the strongest established evidence. The next experiment must fix the manipulation (implement If-None-Match → 304 in the client), match parent power (n ≥ 480), and log cache hit rate as an artifact to enable causal attribution.
